newsitem.title: BURMA: Suu Kyi says Burma still holds people after unrest.
newsitem.headline: Suu Kyi says Burma still holds people after unrest.

text.p: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi said on Monday the military government still held 105 people after anti-government street protests in December.
Suu Kyi said the detainees comprised 24 students, 34 members and supporters of her National League for Democracy (NLD) party, 18 NLD youths and 29 non-NLD members.

The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) said last Saturday no more detainees were held in connection with the student-led unrest, the most serious since the 1988 pro-democracy movement that was crushed by the military.
The Nobel laureate condemned closed trials of detainees by the government and the lack of legal counsel for defendants.
"They should not be afraid to allow defendants to have counsel if they have evidence against them that is solid."
The government recently announced that 34 people, including some NLD members, had been jailed in connection with the student unrest without mentioning trials.
Suu Kyi told a news conference that she did not need the government to look after her personal security.
The SLORC has said that public access to Suu Kyi has been blocked because it wants to safeguard her security. It said such barriers would be removed only after the situation improved.

Suu Kyi said that instead she needed protection against government members, saying she had heard reliably that a cabinet minister had urged a state-sponsored organisation to eliminate her at around the time her motorcade was attacked by an unknown group last November.
"The people from whom they will have to protect me from are those in fact who are in authority," she said.
Suu Kyi repeated earlier calls to foreign investors to shun Burma until freedom and democracy were restored.
"We think that there should be no investment in a country where there is no rule of the law."
PepsiCo Inc, which last year sold its 40 percent stake in a Burmese venture after pressure from human rights groups, said last Tuesday it would cease all ties with Burma.
